title: The Last Delivery, Ep 1: Wrong Address
logline: A broke courier and a glitchy delivery robot open a parcel addressed to someone who died ten years ago.
trend_basis: Hidden-identity reveals dominate top AI drama titles
Episodic shorts ending on a cliffhanger get repeat viewers
original_twist: The secret identity belongs to the parcel, not a person: each episode's package rewrites what Mira knows about her own family.

series.title: The Last Delivery
series.season_arc: Mira traces a chain of impossible parcels back to her missing mother.
series.cliffhanger: The parcel contains Mira's own childhood photo, dated next week.

story.opening_hook: A parcel on a rainy doorstep starts ticking, with the label reading a name crossed out in red.

acts.name: Hook
acts.summary: The ticking parcel and the dead man's name.

acts.name: Build
acts.summary: Mira argues with Tik about opening it; the house has been empty for years.

story.ending: Mira stares at a photo of herself as a child, stamped with next week's date, as the house lights switch on behind her.
hook_variants: Open on Mira's shocked face lit by the house lights, then cut back to the doorstep: 'Ten minutes earlier.'
Open on the robot saying 'Recipient is inside' while pointing its lens at a boarded-up door.

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, night, heavy rain. Extreme close-up of a brown paper parcel on a wet stone doorstep, a shipping label with a name crossed out in red ink, the parcel trembling slightly. Slow push-in, cold blue streetlight.
shots.on_screen_text: This parcel is for a dead man.

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, night, heavy rain. Mira, a 19-year-old Indian woman with a short black bob haircut, a thin scar through her left eyebrow, wearing an oversized yellow raincoat over a grey hoodie crouches by a parcel on the doorstep of a dark abandoned house. Beside her is Tik, a knee-high rusty orange delivery robot with one cracked round blue eye-lens and a dented boxy body on two small wheels. She says, annoyed: "Nobody has lived here for ten years, Tik." The robot's lens flickers. Medium two-shot, handheld, blue streetlight.
shots.dialogue: Mira: Nobody has lived here for ten years, Tik.

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, night, heavy rain. Close-up of Tik, a knee-high rusty orange delivery robot with one cracked round blue eye-lens and a dented boxy body on two small wheels, tilting its body upward. It says in a chirpy synthetic voice: "Delivery must be completed. Recipient is inside." Rain streaks down its lens, a window glows faintly behind it.
shots.dialogue: Tik: Delivery must be completed. Recipient is inside.

shots.prompt: Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, night, heavy rain. Mira, a 19-year-old Indian woman with a short black bob haircut, a thin scar through her left eyebrow, wearing an oversized yellow raincoat over a grey hoodie looks up slowly at a dark upstairs window of the abandoned house, fear replacing her smirk. Low angle, slow tilt up from her face to the window.

Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, night, heavy rain. Mira, a 19-year-old Indian woman with a short black bob haircut, a thin scar through her left eyebrow, wearing an oversized yellow raincoat over a grey hoodie tears open a brown paper parcel with shaking hands and pulls out a faded photograph. Over-the-shoulder shot, shallow focus on her hands.

Vertical 9:16, cinematic realism, night, heavy rain. Close-up of a faded photograph of a small girl in a yellow raincoat, a date stamp in the corner, held in wet fingers. Rack focus to Mira, a 19-year-old Indian woman with a short black bob haircut, a thin scar through her left eyebrow, wearing an oversized yellow raincoat over a grey hoodie, her face frozen in shock, as warm lights switch on in the house behind her.
shots.voiceover: Mira: That's me. And that date... is next week.
